<action type="say">
Given what was in your wallet, here’s what to prioritize, in order:

1) Your other banks’ debit cards (do this right away)  
- Call each bank’s lost/stolen number (usually on their website/mobile app).  
- Ask them to:  
  - Immediately block the stolen debit card.  
  - Issue a replacement card.  
  - Review recent activity and flag any suspicious or ATM withdrawals you don’t recognize.  
- If those cards are linked to checking accounts with higher balances, ask about:  
  - Daily ATM and purchase limits.  
  - Whether they recommend a temporary account freeze or monitoring.

2) Your driver’s license / state ID  
- Report it lost/stolen to your DMV and request a replacement.  
- Ask if they note the license as “stolen” in their system.  
- Because your ID + cards were together, consider:  
  - Placing a fraud alert or credit freeze with the major credit bureaus so new credit can’t be opened easily in your name.

3) Your health insurance card  
- Contact your health insurer’s member services.  
- Tell them your card was stolen and request a new ID card/number if they support that.  
- Ask them to monitor for unusual claims or provider usage under your name.

4) Identity / credit protection (same day or next)  
- Place at least a fraud alert with one major credit bureau (they usually notify the others).  
- Over the next few months, check your credit reports for:  
  - New accounts or inquiries you don’t recognize.

5) Clean-up once replacements arrive  
- Update any direct deposits or automatic payments tied to those other bank accounts (if needed).  
- Store photos/record of your wallet contents somewhere secure for the future.

<action type="say">
Here are concise call scripts and asks for each bank. You can literally read these to the rep.

**For Chase (debit card)**  
When they answer, say:  
- “I need to report my debit card as stolen.”  
- “My wallet was stolen and this card was inside. Please immediately block this card so it can’t be used.”  
- “Please issue me a replacement debit card and let me know how long it will take to arrive.”  
- “Can you review my recent transactions and ATM withdrawals and tell me if you see anything suspicious? I want to dispute any unauthorized activity.”  
- “Do you recommend any temporary protections on my account, like limiting or monitoring certain transactions, given that my ID and other cards were stolen with this card?”  
- “Will my PIN stay the same, or can you issue a new PIN with the replacement card?”  

Specific things to **ask for**:  
- Card immediately blocked.  
- Replacement card issued (and shipping timeframe).  
- Review of recent activity and filing disputes if anything is unauthorized.  
- Clarification on fraud liability and how to report anything new that appears later.  
- Whether they advise a temporary account hold, lower limits, or any extra monitoring.  
- New PIN option if you’re at all worried it could have been seen or compromised.

**For Bank of America (debit card)**  
When they answer, say:  
- “I need to report my debit card as stolen.”  
- “My wallet was stolen and this card was inside. Please immediately block this card so it can’t be used.”  
- “Please send me a replacement debit card and tell me how long it should take to arrive.”  
- “Can you review the recent transactions and ATM withdrawals on this account with me and help me dispute anything that isn’t mine?”  
- “Because my driver’s license and health insurance card were also in the stolen wallet, do you recommend any additional protections on my account?”  
- “Will a new PIN be issued with the replacement card, or can you reset my PIN as part of this?”  

Specific things to **ask for**:  
- Immediate block of the stolen debit card.  
- Replacement debit card (and expedited shipping options, if available).  
- Review + dispute of any suspicious or unauthorized transactions.  
- Explanation of their fraud protection policy and any provisional credits.  
- Any extra protections they can add (alerts, limits, monitoring, or temporary holds).  
- New or reset PIN with the replacement card.

If you want, you can paste these into a note app and check each bullet off as you talk to them.</action>
